QueryOptions.description:
Optional query parameters for fine-tuning retrieval.

`extra='forbid'` is load-bearing, not tidiness. Pydantic's default is
`extra='ignore'`, and under it a client sent `search_mode: 'hybrid'` for months
while the engine silently dropped it: the "hybrid fallback" re-ran the
identical dense query, scored the identical chunks, and reported success.
Every layer said it worked. An unknown field is now a 422, so a caller that
is out of step with this engine fails loudly instead of degrading quietly.

category_weights.description:
How much this caller trusts each content category, as a multiplier on the final score. Applied after every ranking stage and BEFORE the trim to `final_k`, so a weight can promote a chunk into the answer or drop one out of it. A category not listed here — and a chunk with no category at all — is weighted 1.0: an omission means no opinion, never a demotion.

Choose the magnitude deliberately. Scores are RRF, and RRF is a narrow band: rank 1 scores 1/61 and rank 20 scores 1/80, a spread of only 1.3x. So 0.5 does not 'slightly prefer' — it outweighs the entire ranking. Use values near 1.0 (0.9/1.1) for a nudge and reserve aggressive values for a category you genuinely want overridden.
category_weights.title: Category Weights

enable_hyde.description: Enable HyDE for this query (overrides default).
enable_hyde.title: Enable Hyde

final_k.description: How many chunks are returned, after every ranking stage has run. This is the knob a caller sizing a context window actually wants. Omit to use the corpus setting, then the engine default. Bounded above by what survives the pipeline: `top_k` candidates, and when reranking is on, `RAG_RERANK_TOP_K_OUTPUT` (10 by default) — ask for 12 and you get 10.
final_k.title: Final K

metadata_filters.description: Arbitrary key-value filters applied to document metadata.
metadata_filters.title: Metadata Filters

search_mode.description: Retrieval mode. 'dense' = vector similarity only. 'hybrid' = vector fused with BM25 keyword search, which is what finds exact identifiers (SKU, order number, box code) that carry little semantic signal. 'keyword' = BM25 alone, with no embedding call: exact lookups. Omit to use the corpus setting, then the engine default.
search_mode.title: Search Mode

top_k.description: RETRIEVAL WIDTH — how many candidates each query vector pulls from the index, before fusion, reranking, MMR and decay. This is NOT the number of chunks you get back; that is `final_k`. Setting this to the number of chunks you want collapses the funnel, because every ranking stage downstream can only reorder what search already handed it. Leave it alone unless you are deliberately trading recall for latency.
top_k.title: Top K

user_id.description: Filter by user ID (for memory scoping).
user_id.title: User Id

hybrid_search_enabled.description: Fuse a BM25 sparse leg into the query pipeline alongside dense search. Engine default on. Dense embeddings are weakest on exact identifiers — SKUs, order numbers, box codes — which is what BM25 is best at.

pipeline_order_enabled.description: Deliver chunks in the order the pipeline decided, carrying each stage's own score on `score`. Off, rerank/MMR/decay reorder the list and context assembly re-sorts it back by the RRF fusion score, discarding the cross-encoder's ordering. Engine default off: it changes both the ordering and the `score` number every caller sees. `score_breakdown.fused_score` carries the raw fusion score either way, so the two orderings stay comparable.
pipeline_order_enabled.title: Pipeline Order Enabled

preset.description: Named preset: 'economy' (fast/cheap), 'standard' (balanced), 'premium' (max quality). When set, all retrieval fields are populated from the preset. Individual field overrides below take priority over preset values.

rerank_llm_model.title: Rerank Llm Model

rerank_provider.description: Which reranker to use. 'local' is the self-hosted cross-encoder: free, runs on this box, and its speed depends entirely on the device — measured 406ms on GPU and 9.7s on CPU for a real 20-candidate query. 'llm' ranks with the credentials the caller sends on the X-LLM-* headers, and is billed per query to whoever owns that key; it is 4-8x faster than the CPU path but slower than the GPU one, which no network call can beat. A failure on 'llm' falls back to 'local' rather than turning reranking off. A value outside this set is a 422 rather than a silent fallback to the default.
rerank_provider.title: Rerank Provider

top_k.description: Retrieval width — candidates pulled per query vector, before fusion, reranking, MMR and decay. NOT the number of chunks returned; that is `final_k`. This field was documented as 'final chunks returned' for a long time, which is how at least one corpus ended up pinned to 5 and silently lost its whole rerank funnel.

the prompt budget; here it would only cut such searches short.

ScoreBreakdown.description:
Per-stage detail behind a chunk's single `score`.

`score` is the RRF fusion score, and every stage after fusion only reorders —
it never rewrites that number. So the score alone cannot say whether a chunk
arrived by dense similarity, by an exact keyword hit, or because the
cross-encoder rescued it. A `null` field means the stage did not run.

age_days.description: Chunk age in days, as measured for decay. Null when decay is off.
age_days.title: Age Days

category.description: The chunk's content category, as indexed. Null if it has none.
category.title: Category

category_weight.description: The multiplier applied from `category_weights`. Null when the caller sent none; 1.0 when it sent some but had no opinion on this category.
category_weight.title: Category Weight

decay_multiplier.description: Temporal decay factor in (0, 1]. Null when decay is off.
decay_multiplier.title: Decay Multiplier

dense_rank.description: Best 1-indexed rank this chunk reached in any dense (vector) leg. Null means dense search never returned it — it came from BM25 alone.
dense_rank.title: Dense Rank

dense_score.description: Cosine similarity to the query in the dense leg (best across query variants). Null when dense search did not return this chunk.
dense_score.title: Dense Score

fused_score.description: Score after fusing the search legs — convex (weighted, normalized) by default, RRF if the corpus chose it. Equals `score` unless `category_weights` was sent, in which case `score` is this times `category_weight`.
fused_score.title: Fused Score

pipeline_rank.description: 1-indexed position after every ranking stage (rerank, MMR, decay). Note this need NOT match the chunk's position in `chunks`: context assembly re-sorts by `score`, which is the pre-rerank fusion score.
pipeline_rank.title: Pipeline Rank

rerank_score.description: Cross-encoder score. Null when reranking is off or it failed.
rerank_score.title: Rerank Score

sparse_rank.description: 1-indexed rank in the BM25 leg. Null when hybrid search is off for this query, or when BM25 did not return this chunk.
sparse_rank.title: Sparse Rank

sparse_score.description: BM25 score in the keyword leg. Null when that leg did not return it.
sparse_score.title: Sparse Score

ScoreBreakdown.title: ScoreBreakdown

and files), members, and the accounts that belonged only to it. Any status.

`max_corpora` overrides the plan's knowledge-base limit; `null` removes the override.
Lowering it below the tenant's count blocks new knowledge bases only.

`is_active: false` suspends an active tenant and needs `confirm_name` (its current
name) in the same body; `true` reactivates a suspended one. A value the tenant
already has changes nothing. A pending tenant is activated with `POST .../activate`.

Decline a pending sign-up: the tenant and its sign-up account are removed and
the owner gets a polite e-mail (the reason stays in the audit log).

The response carries `accept_url`: send it yourself if the engine has no SMTP (the
e-mail goes out too when it does), e.g. to onboard a customer's owner in closed mode.

Delete a document, all its versions, chunks, and vectors.

Purges the document's vectors from Qdrant (every version) and deletes the
Document row, which cascades to versions -> chunks -> embeddings and chunk
metadata in Postgres. Idempotent re-ingestion (e.g. after a chunker change)
relies on this: the pipeline dedups byte-identical content by fingerprint,

Publish a post-ingest review as a new version of the reviewed document.

The workspace's accepted chunks (everything not rejected) become a new active
version, embedded and indexed like an ingest; the reviewed version is kept inactive
(restorable) and its vectors are removed. 409 `wrong_workspace_kind` for a workspace
not created from an ingested document, `invalid_status_transition` when already
finalized, `workspace_locked` when someone else holds the edit lock,
`version_not_active` when the document changed since the review began,
`reviewed_document_deleted` when it was deleted, `document_busy` when an ingest or
restore of the document holds it for more than a few seconds, `review_changed` when
chunks were edited while the new version was being built; 422
`nothing_to_finalize` when every chunk was rejected; 503 `finalize_failed` when
embedding or the vector store failed (nothing is changed).

post.description: Execute a query against the corpus and return a generated answer.

Retrieval-only endpoint — returns ranked chunks without LLM generation.

Use this when the caller has its own LLM and only needs relevant document
chunks as context. Runs steps 1-13 of the query pipeline (embedding,
vector search, reranking, context assembly) but skips LLM generation,
validation, and query logging.

Stream an answer as Server-Sent Events, in the widget's named-event format.

Events, in order:

- `sources` — `{"query_id", "sources": [{index, chunk_id, document_id,
  external_id, file_name, section, page, snippet, score}]}`: the citations
  the answer is grounded on, before the first token.
- `token` — `{"content"}`, repeatedly.
- `done` — `{"query_id", "model", "latency_ms", "usage": {prompt_tokens,
  completion_tokens, total_tokens}}`. Token counts are estimates: providers
  report no usage on a stream. `query_id` is logged before `done` is sent,
  so it works for `GET /query/{id}` and feedback straight away.
- `error` — `{"detail"}` replaces the rest if generation fails part-way.

A failure before streaming starts is an ordinary HTTP error, as on /query.
